subject: bmc: sync-once: handle deleted source files

comments.message:
Patch Set 1: Ok-To-Test+1

User approved, CI ok to start

Patch Set 1: Verified+1

Build Successful 

https://jenkins.openbmc.org/job/ci-repository/100797/ : SUCCESS
Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as 7fe19f4d2aa5c31facca05c580ad984885258195

The code already handles deleting the destination files whenever the source files are deleted: https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/blob/85aed223a200a7769a27a281662ce991db09420a/bmc/sync_manager.cpp#L64

```
execl("/usr/bin/rsync", "rsync", "-a", "--delete",
```

The commit message says this change will handle the scenario when source files are deleted, but what's being proposed instead is doing a one-time blind delete of files in the destination directory that don't exist in the source directory before the sync manager starts up. This is not what we want.

One example could be that the current flash device ran out of space and it's non-responsive, so the customer performs a factory reset which wipes out all the data. Then with the existing code they can switch to the alternate flash and all their previous synced data would still be there as expected (the sync manager is a form of backup).
With this proposed change, we'd delete all the data from the alternate flash when the BMC starts up just because it didn't exist in the current flash, which could be empty because of factory reset, or chip replacement, etc.

> The code already handles deleting the destination files whenever the source files are deleted

Yup,  What I meant here is the second scenario, `such as a factory reset`.

What I expect is that the configuration in the backup should be exactly the same as the main flash (as long as the main flash has been booted normally). Even if the configuration in the main flash is empty, they should mirror each other.

I encountered a case like this:
We have a network configuration in the `settingsd`  that needs to be synchronized (related to ncsi/rj45 port selection). The` settingsd` configuration will have a `default code` value, and when modified, it generates a file and synchronizes it.

When the default code is set to rj45 and the cable is connected to the rj45 port, everything works fine. However, when someone mistakenly sets it to ncsi, it causes a disconnection. 
A `factory reset` might restore its operation, but because the second image retains the incorrect ncsi configuration, it may cause the second image to lose connection the next time it's booted.

Of course, this is just an example . It highlights that if we don't perform deletion, synchronizing certain configurations could result in mismatched configurations between the two images, leading to unexpected issues.

I see your point, although I'm still concerned that we'd not support the case anymore that I pointed out about after a factory reset I do want to boot from the second image and have all the previous data present because the data is good and useful to get the system back to where it was before.

In the case you described, perhaps the settingsd code could generate an empty file or a file with some default value if none is present, that'd cause the sync to trigger and overwrite the file in the alternate version.

If that's not viable, I guess we could go with your change, although I'd like to see if Lei has any opinions since he may be using systems with the static layout to make sure we don't break other people's use cases.
